Start a montage

Source: R/tidymontage.R
tidymontage.Rd

tidymontage() turns a tibble of images into a montage. Like tidyplot() in tidyplots, it takes the mapping and the size; add_*() and adjust_*() verbs then add merges, crops, zooms, scale bars and more. Nothing is read from disk until the montage is printed or saved.

Usage

tidymontage(
  images,
  x = NULL,
  y = NULL,
  ...,
  layout = "grid",
  gap = NULL,
  width = NULL,
  height = NULL,
  units = NULL
)

Arguments

images

A data frame of images, usually from read_images(). Must contain the columns filepath, channel and img.

x, y

Columns mapped to the columns (x) and rows (y) of the montage: a bare name such as condition, or several with c() (the first one varies slowest). In the grid layout, channel and view can be mapped too.

...

Choose and order the levels of panel dimensions, for example channel = c("GFP", "DAPI") or condition = "ctrl".

layout

"grid" (the default) or "hero", or a layout created with layout_grid() or layout_hero().

gap

Gap between panels in mm. NULL (the default) uses tidymontage_options(), or 1.

width, height, units

Size of the box the panel grid fits into, see adjust_size(). NULL (the default) uses tidymontage_options(), or 90 x 90 mm.

Value

A tidymontage object. Printing it draws the montage.

Details

The images tibble decides which images are shown: select planes with filter() and project z-stacks with summarise(img = max(img)) before calling tidymontage(). Everything visual is decided by the montage.

Columns mapped to x and y (such as condition) arrange blocks of panels. Within each block, the layout arranges channels and views (see layout_grid()); in the grid, map channel or view to x or y to place them yourself. Merges and zooms added later become levels of channel and view. Each panel must show exactly one image.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
read_images(c("ctrl.ome.tif", "ko.ome.tif")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(condition = ifelse(grepl("ctrl", filepath), "ctrl", "ko")) |>
  tidymontage(x = condition)
} # }
